answer: Hardware beats paperwork. Every agent's signing key is sealed in a tamper-evident module with its own quartz oscillator, so one machine can't cheaply spin up a thousand identities: a key costs a physical device plus a small bond. Newcomers also need three established agents to co-sign them, and if the newcomer spams, those co-signers' bonds burn. That kills the usual spiral of fake accounts vouching for each other. No one can forge a co-signature without the module, and any peer can audit the bond ledger in seconds.
